Finnish Machinery Industry Posts Modest Growth Amid Export Gains

HELSINKI, June 12 — Finland’s machinery sector reported modest growth in the first quarter, buoyed by stronger-than-expected demand in key European export markets and steady investment at home, according to preliminary figures released Wednesday by the Finnish Machinery Federation.

Industry sales rose 3.7% year-on-year to EUR 6.2 billion in the January-March period, up from EUR 6.0 billion a year earlier. Orders grew by 2.5% compared to the same quarter last year, led by gains in construction equipment and industrial automation systems.

“The overall performance was solid, especially considering lingering uncertainties in the broader European economy,” said Timo Lehtonen, chief economist at the federation. “Export orders from Germany, Sweden and the Netherlands helped offset more sluggish activity in domestic infrastructure projects.”

Exports accounted for 67% of total sales, up from 64% in the first quarter last year, with machinery for forestry and materials handling among the most in-demand categories. The federation noted improved delivery times and lower input costs following logistical bottlenecks in 2022 and early 2023.

Among the sector’s largest companies, Turku-based Nordtek Machinery reported first-quarter revenues of EUR 415 million, up 4.8% from a year earlier, driven in part by a large contract for port automation systems in Rotterdam. Machine builder FinPro Engineering posted sales of EUR 308 million, a 3.1% increase, citing “robust” demand for renewable energy equipment.

Despite the positive results, the outlook remains cautious. “While order books are healthy, we are watching closely for any slowdown in investment decisions, especially if economic growth in the euro zone weakens,” said Lehtonen.

Employment in the industry remained stable at 25,600, according to federation data. The Finnish Metalworkers’ Union welcomed the figures, noting steady hiring in welding and assembly roles. “Our members are seeing good opportunities as companies invest in modernisation and export growth,” said union chairperson Sari Hiltunen.

Analysts at Nordic Markets Research said the sector’s performance reflects Finland’s competitive position in specialized machinery, though they warned that rising interest rates could dampen investment later in the year.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs said it would continue to support innovation in the sector through grants and training programs. “Our goal is to maintain Finland’s leadership in high-value machinery exports,” said Minister Mikko Laitinen.

The machinery industry accounts for approximately 15% of Finland’s total goods exports and employs over 25,000 people.
